info.bio:
Sparklehorse fue el seudónimo de Mark Linkous, vocalista y multi instrumentista, fallecido en marzo de 2010 por suicidio.
 Ya en 1996, durante una gira por Europa con Radiohead, después de editar su 1º disco, "Vivadixiesubmarinetransmissionplot", Linkous sufrió una sobredosis con una combinación de antidepresivos, Valium, alcohol y heroína en una habitación de hotel en Londres. Inconsciente y con las piernas aplastadas por él mismo durante casi catorce horas

scenes.name: Cantautores lo-fi de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los noventa son la década del cantautor: la tecnología y las redes informales del post-punk favorecen la carrera en solitario, con Joni Mitchell y Leonard Cohen (no Dylan ni Springsteen) como maestros. El folk sombrío inaugurado por Chris Isaak, Smog y American Music Club se convierte casi en un género: Vic Chesnutt, Mark Lanegan, Mountain Goats, Elliott Smith, Jeff Buckley, Ron Sexsmith, Mike Johnson, Simon Joyner, Songs:Ohia. El neo-pop de Stephen Merritt (Magnetic Fields: Holiday, The Charm Of The Highway Strip, 69 Love Songs), Chris Connelly, Frank Black, Mike Gira (Body Lovers, Angels Of Light), Richard Davies y Eric Matthews (Cardinal), David Gray. El neo-folk de Beck (folk para la era del hip hop), John Frusciante, Sparklehorse, Bright Eyes, Rufus Wainwright, Grandaddy, Bobby Conn; el neo-country de Richard Buckner y Freedy Johnston; Steve Wynn, Mike Watt, Paul Westerberg, Ben Harper.

podcast.title: Drug Overdose and Its Aftermath
podcast.body: During a European tour with Radiohead following the release of their debut album, Mark Linkous suffered a severe overdose of antidepressants, Valium, and heroin, exacerbated by alcohol consumption. He was found 14 hours later in his London hotel bathroom, having passed out with his legs pinned, which led to a build-up of potassium that caused his heart to stop. Although revived and undergoing surgery, he lost the use of both legs for six months, requiring a wheelchair, and developed kidney failure, necessitating dialysis for the rest of his life. "Here Mark Linkhouse O.D. and he depressants, valium, and heroin all washed down with a lot of alcohol."

podcast.title: Frontman's Reputation
podcast.body: Sparklehorse was led by Mark Linkous, a highly respected songwriter from Richmond, Virginia. He garnered admiration from various notable artists and bands, including The Flaming Lips, Metric, The Silver Sun Pickups, and Patti Smith. "The group was Sparkle Horse. And they were led by a very well-regarded songwriter from Richmond, Virginia, named Mark Linkhouse."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Impact on Songwriting
podcast.body: Mark Linkous's near-fatal overdose and subsequent health issues profoundly impacted his perspective and songwriting, which became noticeably "darker and more somber." Despite his struggles, he continued to create music for Sparklehorse and contributed to various TV and film projects. "This affected his outlook in a songwriting, which became darker and more somber."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Tragic Suicide
podcast.body: Mark Linkous's battle with depression persisted despite his continued musical work. While in the process of divorcing his wife of 19 years, he took his own life in Knoxville, Tennessee. He used a rifle, aiming it at his heart, and at the time of his death, he had a blood alcohol level of .43, with various antidepressants and anti-anxiety medications found in his system. "Then, while on the process of a divorce from his wife of 19 years, he took a rifle, went for a walk, sat down on an alley in Knoxville, Tennessee, aimed the gun at his heart and pulled the trigger."

xref.title: Tour with Sparklehorse
xref.body: Radiohead embarked on a European tour with Sparklehorse following the release of Sparklehorse's debut album *Vivadixie Submarine Transmission Plot*. This tour was unfortunately the setting for Mark Linkous's near-fatal overdose. "Their debut album was enough to land them on a European tour with Radiohead."
